Specification: abs

1. Overview
    abs is a total function on the integers. It maps each integer x
    to its absolute value, defined by cases on the sign of x.

2. Signature
    abs : Z -> Z

3. Definition
    For all x in Z:

        | x       if x >= 0
    abs(x) = {
        | -x      otherwise (i.e., if x < 0)

4. Expected Properties
    P1. Non-negativity:
            For all x in Z:  abs(x) >= 0

    P2. Case identity (non-negative input):
            For all x in Z:  x >= 0  =>  abs(x) = x

    P3. Case identity (negative input):
            For all x in Z:  x < 0   =>  abs(x) = -x

5. Remarks
    - Properties P1-P3 together characterize abs completely: every
      integer maps to exactly one value satisfying them, so any
      implementation meeting P1-P3 is correct.
    - Note that abs(0) = 0, and for x != 0, abs(x) > 0.
